The child who dashes ahead when in a hurry

When they see somewhere they want to go, kids forget to look both ways or check the signal and run straight ahead. Many parents have felt that heart-stopping moment when a hand slips free. On the road, a single moment of carelessness can lead to a serious accident.

Kids dash out not because they don't know the danger, but because their eagerness runs ahead of them. That's why traffic safety needs habits that make the body stop automatically, no matter how hurried, more than the words 'be careful.'

Curious about the plot of this traffic-safety story for kids? Explore the lesson of the traffic-safety story through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read the traffic-safety story with your child and talk about it together. We've gathered many stories about Stop! Hand Up! Look for Cars! covering crosswalk safety education, traffic-safety picture books, children's safety habits, and more.

content.text:
Why traffic-safety habits matter

Traffic safety is the highest-priority daily habit—one tied directly to your child's life. Safety habits ingrained early protect your child even when you're not by their side.

What matters isn't scaring them, but giving them simple promises they can keep on their own. The three steps—stop, raise your hand, and look for cars before crossing—are easy for a child to memorize, and with repetition they come to mind automatically even in a hurried moment.
content.caption: The three promises: stop, hand up, look for cars before crossing.

content.alt: 16. Stop! Hand Up! Look for Cars! - Hori's three-promises story
content.text:
Hori's three-promises story

In "Stop! Hand Up! Look for Cars!", Hori is in such a rush to get to the playground that he steps into the road without looking both ways. Just as Dad quickly grabs his hand to stop him, a car zooms right past.

Dad says, 'The promise comes before the hurry,' and a smiling little traffic light teaches the three promises. One, stop right at the sidewalk! Two, raise your hand up high! Three, look both ways and cross! When the green light comes on, Hori crosses carefully just as promised, and on the way back he leads the way, calling out the promises himself.
content.caption: The more you're in a hurry, the more the promise comes first.

content.alt: 16. Stop! Hand Up! Look for Cars! - Let's practice together at home
content.text:
Let's practice together at home

After reading, connect the story to the real road. First, rather than scaring them, repeat the three short promises—'stop, hand up, look for cars before crossing'—so your child memorizes them.

Second, emphasize the principle that no matter how hurried, stopping comes first when crossing the road. Third, at a real crosswalk, hold hands and cross while chanting the book's refrain together. With repetition, the safety promises become second nature and come to mind on their own even in a hurried moment.

content.text:
Frequently asked questions

Q. From what age should I teach road crossing?

A. From the age when you walk hand in hand together, you can teach the order—stop, hand up, look for cars before crossing—like a game. Repeating it until it becomes second nature is the most important thing.

Q. Will a traffic-safety story for kids help?

A. By imitating the main character in the story, your child naturally remembers the promises to keep on the road. A traffic-safety story for kids lets them learn crosswalk rules joyfully.

Q. What should I do when my child tries to run into the road?

A. Rather than scolding, calmly explain why they need to stop and set a promise to hold hands tightly. Praising them when they keep it helps the habit of being careful grow on its own.
